This is an out of browser password manager for the terminal. If you know the website and your username and you've configed the salt then you've got a stong password. This is based on the lastpass strong password generator. These are not the only options you could use as any command line argument will go into the password. The extra paranoid can remember simple passwords for each site as you would have to without a manager to use as an additional per-site salt and get back complex strong passwords. That can be helpful if you want the ability to change passwords in the future. Just remember two or three passwords and change them around as you renew passwords on sites. Or you could replace that with a revision number. If you really wanted to you could even forget the username if you just have one main account per site.

Example:

#typical use
pass voat.co luckyguy
#bit more advanced
pass voat luckyguy dadadada #MZ's pass
#revision number
pass voat luckyguy 1 #maybe skip that till you need a revision number.
#Most simple
pass voat

Nice, so it's not really a 'manager' so much as a password generator based on stuff you know, with the salt acting as kind of a master password?

I wrote something similar, but wanted something deterministic so the output would be the same every time, i didn't want to use random anywhere. so i used salt * username * website * password_length cast into a seed number where i'd % through a list of characters until i've reached password_length this also allows me to make a custom array. converting from letters to numbers was by ascii value so SALT = 83+65+76+84

The reason why I wanted to do this was for transparency, things like OnePass/LastPass etc. (so far as I know) don't tell anyone how they generate your password, so if for some reason I can't get to my app which i have on my android and i have a version on my ipad, I could write my own generator quickly if i needed. There's also the fun trick that I could (in theory) make a mechanical version since % is basically a gear.
